articles.title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?
articles.standfirst: How fair are AI recruitment tools that help decide our future, and what happens when we click "apply"?

gist: Jobseekers worry about automated recruitment tools and bias.
Many workers are unaware they can request human reviews.
Recruiters note a surge in AI-written applications.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Jobseekers face automated rejections and growing concerns over AI recruitment tools. A campaign called Reject the Rejections highlights that many workers do not know their legal right to challenge automated decisions. Meanwhile, recruiters report a massive surge in applications, with many candidates using AI to polish or write their submissions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Candidates fear recruitment software introduces bias and lacks human context. Surveys show that many ethnically diverse jobseekers alter their CVs out of fear of rejection. Conversely, recruiters note a perception gap, as candidates believe AI screens CVs far more often than it actually does.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Campaigners and regulators call for greater transparency, audits, and accountability from employers regarding automated hiring systems.

fivew: Jobseekers, recruiters, and organisations like People Like Us.
Jobseekers and employers are navigating the increasing use of artificial intelligence in recruitment.
